big_case_rationale: A clean statutory split on a recurring but narrow immigration-adjustment question affecting former asylees with terminated status; consequential for that class, low public salience.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority reads 'the status of any alien granted asylum' in 8 U.S.C. 1159(b) as describing a present status the alien must hold when adjusting (the status being adjusted is asylee status), resting principally on the parallel use of 'alien granted asylum' in 1158(c)(1) for benefits that end on termination and on the 1990 former-asylee note's express 'regardless of whether or not such asylum has been terminated' carve-out as negative implication; it rejects the past-participle reading and declines to apply immigration lenity because the text is not grievously ambiguous.

The holding is a categorical rule: no alien whose asylum has been terminated may adjust under 1159(b), whatever the reason for termination (including derivative asylees who lose status through a principal), not a holding confined to terminations for particularly serious crimes or to these petitioners' facts.
